Wooldridge's test for serial correlation in a panel

Source: R/dpnl.R
wsctst.Rd

Whether the idiosyncratic errors of a linear panel model with unit effects are serially correlated, by the test Wooldridge (2002) derives and Drukker (2003) sets out and evaluates, the test Andreatta et al. (2023, p. 1373) run on the residuals of their static models before choosing a dynamic one. The first differences of y are regressed on those of x, without a constant, which differencing removes (Drukker 2003, sec. 2); without serial correlation the residuals e_it of consecutive differences correlate at -0.5, so e_it is regressed on e_i,t-1 with the variance clustered by unit, and the coefficient is tested against -0.5: F = ((coef + 0.5) / se)^2 on 1 and G - 1 degrees of freedom, G the units with a pair. A difference needs the period before, so a gap removes two differences and the pairs that use them. Drukker does not say whether the second regression has a constant; cons = FALSE (the default) leaves it out, since the residuals of the first have none to absorb.

Usage

wsctst(y, x = NULL, unit, time, cons = FALSE, ssc = "cr1")

Arguments

y

The outcome of each row: finite numbers.

x

NULL or the regressors: a numeric matrix or data frame, one row per row of y.

unit

The unit of each row: labels.

time

The period of each row: numbers; each unit at most once per period.

cons

TRUE for a constant in the regression of the residual on its lag.

ssc

"cr1" or "none": the small-sample factor of the variance.

Value

An object of class wsctst, a list: stat, a named vector (F, df1, df2, p, coef the coefficient of the lagged residual, se, pairs, clusters, ndiff the differences); coef, the differenced regression (term, est, se), NULL without x; and ssc.

References

Drukker, D. M. (2003). Testing for serial correlation in linear panel-data models. The Stata Journal, 3(2), 168-177. doi:10.1177/1536867X0300300206

Wooldridge, J. M. (2002). Econometric Analysis of Cross Section and Panel Data. MIT Press.

Andreatta, D., Favarin, S., Lisciandra, M. and Millemaci, E. (2023). Digging into waste: an analysis of waste crime in the Italian provinces. Regional Studies, 57(7), 1367-1379. doi:10.1080/00343404.2022.2135697

Examples

set.seed(8)
d <- expand.grid(year = 1:8, prov = paste0("p", 1:40))
d$x <- rnorm(320)
d$e <- 0
for (i in which(d$year > 1)) d$e[i] <- 0.6 * d$e[i - 1] + rnorm(1)
d$y <- d$x + rnorm(40)[as.integer(substring(d$prov, 2))] + d$e
wsctst(d$y, d["x"], d$prov, d$year)
#> wsctst: Wooldridge test of serial correlation, F(1, 39) = 5.1486, p 0.02888
#> lagged residual -0.3814 (se 0.05228; -0.5 without correlation), 240 pairs
